ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A horizontal platform of height $H=0.4m$ is placed on a level ground, on which a rough straight track $AB$ with an inclination angle of $\theta=37^{\circ}$, a horizontal smooth straight track $BC$, a quarter-circular smooth thin circular pipe $CD$, and a semi-circular smooth track $DEF$ are vertically placed, and they are smoothly connected. The radius of the pipe $CD$ is $r=0.1m$ with its center at point $O_{1}$, and the radius of the track $DEF$ is $R=0.2m$ with its center at point $O_{2}$. Points $O_{1}$, $D$, $O_{2}$, and $F$ are all on the same horizontal line. A small slider starts from rest at point $P$ on the track $AB$, which is at a height $h$ above the platform, and slides down. It undergoes an elastic collision with a small ball of equal mass at rest on the track $BC$. After the collision, the small ball passes through the pipe $CD$ and the track $DEF$, moving vertically downwards from point $F$ and collides with a triangular prism $G$ fixed on a straight rod directly below. After the collision, the ball's velocity direction is horizontal to the right, and its magnitude is the same as before the collision. Finally, it lands at point $Q$ on the ground. The coefficient of kinetic friction between the slider and the track $AB$ is $\mu=\frac{1}{12}$, $\sin37^{\circ}=0.6$, and $\cos37^{\circ}=0.8$.

1. If the initial height of the slider is $h=0.9m$, calculate the magnitude of the velocity $v_{0}$ of the slider when it reaches point $B$.
2. If the small ball can complete the entire motion process, determine the minimum value of $h$, denoted as $h_{min}$.
3. If the small ball just barely passes the highest point $E$, and the position of the triangular prism $G$ is adjustable vertically, calculate the maximum horizontal distance $x_{max}$ between the landing point $Q$ and point $F$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: In the figure, the left inclined track AB is placed on a horizontal platform, point P is above the inclined plane, the height from P to the platform is marked as h, and the inclined track and the horizontal track BC are smoothly connected near B, with an inclination angle of θ. BC is the horizontal track on the platform, and to the right of C is connected a quarter-circular tube CD, whose radius r and center O1 are marked in the figure; from D it is then connected to a semicircular track DEF, whose highest point is E, center is O2, and radius is R. In the figure, O1, D, O2, and F are at the same horizontal height; F is on the right, the ball moves vertically downward from F, and below there is a triangular prism G that can be adjusted up and down. After collision, it flies out horizontally to the right and lands on the ground at Q, with the horizontal distance marked as x. The height of the platform relative to the ground is marked as H. Then reason: take g=10 m/s^2. 1) The slider slides down from P to B along the rough inclined plane, with a descending height of h, and the length of the inclined plane is s=h/sinθ. The magnitude of friction is μmgcosθ, and the work done by friction is -μmgcosθ·h/sinθ. By the kinetic energy theorem: 1/2 mv_B^2=mgh-μmgcosθ·h/sinθ=mgh(1-μcotθ). Among them cot37°=0.8/0.6=4/3, μcotθ=(1/12)(4/3)=1/9, so 1-μcotθ=8/9. When h=0.9 m, v_B^2=2×10×0.9×8/9=16, therefore v_0=v_B=4 m/s. 2) In an elastic collision of equal masses, the moving slider and the stationary small ball exchange speeds, so after collision the small ball obtains speed v_C=v_B at C. For the small ball to complete the subsequent motion, the limiting condition is at the highest point E of the semicircular track; when critically passing the highest point, v_E^2=gR. From C to E, mechanical energy is conserved on the smooth track. From C to D/F the horizontal height rises by r, and from D/F to E it rises further by R, with a total rise of r+R: 1/2 mv_C^2=mg(r+R)+1/2 mv_E^2. Substituting the critical v_E^2=gR gives v_C^2=2g(r+R)+gR=2gr+3gR. Also v_C^2=2gh(1-μcotθ)=2gh·8/9. Substituting r=0.1 m, R=0.2 m: 2gr+3gR=2×10×0.1+3×10×0.2=2+6=8. Therefore 2×10×h×8/9=8, solving gives h_min=0.45 m. 3) When the small ball just passes the highest point E, v_E^2=gR. From E to F, it descends by height R, and by conservation of mechanical energy: v_F^2=v_E^2+2gR=3gR=3×10×0.2=6. The height of point F is the platform height plus the rise height of CD, namely L=H+r=0.4+0.1=0.5 m. Suppose G is located y below F, then the ball falls y from F to G, and the square of its speed before collision is v_F^2+2gy; after collision, the magnitude of the speed remains unchanged and the direction is horizontal to the right. After collision, it is projected horizontally from height L-y, the flight time t=sqrt[2(L-y)/g], and the horizontal distance satisfies x^2=(v_F^2+2gy)·2(L-y)/g. Let f(y)=x^2, and differentiate with respect to y: f'(y)=4(L-y)-2(v_F^2+2gy)/g=4L-8y-2v_F^2/g. Let f'(y)=0, obtaining y=L/2-v_F^2/(4g)=0.5/2-6/(40)=0.25-0.15=0.10 m, within the allowable range. At this time x^2=(6+2×10×0.1)×2(0.5-0.1)/10=8×0.08=0.64, so x_max=0.8 m.
